title: A Mysterious But Powerful Way To Improve Listening istening/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin moves past mechanical listening tips like volume, pacing, and eye contact to argue that the single most important factor in whether students listen is conviction — the felt belief behind a teacher's words. He explains that authentic conviction cannot be manufactured through confidence tricks or a deeper voice; it can only come from consistently doing what you say you're going to do. Every broken promise or unenforced consequence, he argues, weakens a teacher's credibility both in students' eyes and their own. Linsin describes the resulting effect as an almost physical 'aura' that causes students to lean in and take a teacher's words seriously. The piece is short but makes a clear causal claim: follow-through is what produces the intangible authority that makes students actually listen.
points: The most important, if least obvious, factor in getting students to listen isn't technique — it's conviction, the genuine belief behind a teacher's words.
Conviction cannot be faked through confidence tricks, tone of voice, or self-persuasion; it has to be earned.
Conviction comes specifically from consistency and follow-through — doing what you say you're going to do, every time.
Every broken promise or unenforced consequence weakens a teacher's influence and erodes trust, in students' eyes and the teacher's own.
Teachers with authentic conviction develop a distinctive quality of speech that causes students to lean in and listen closely.
quotes: But what we have yet to cover is perhaps the single most important key to improving listening.
In fact, why it works so well is a bit of a mystery. Because, you see, it’s not about what you do. It’s about what you believe.
It comes from doing what you say you’re going to do. It comes from your consistency and follow through.
For every time you go back on your word or let misbehavior go without the consequence you promised, you weaken your influence and lose trust in the eyes of your students.
There is an unmistakable aura that accompanies teachers with authentic conviction, a distinct vibration of speech that is borne of the perfect symmetry between words and actions.
Do what you say and when you say you’re going to do it, and you’ll speak with a mysterious power that can move mountains.
